title: Failover simulation framework + snapshot reconciliation tests for active-passive DR
creator: Lina Martinez
description: Design and implement a reusable failover simulation framework plus a set of snapshot reconciliation tests targeted at active-passive DR scenarios for Redwood's inference platform. The framework will enable scheduled drills that exercise: topology switchover, tokenstore and KV-cache snapshot restore, canary fencing (circuit-breaker toggles), and load-shedding policies while measuring SLOs and alert fidelity. Deliverables include automation harness, runbook updates, deterministic validation checks for restored data, and observability dashboards for drill metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Automated drill harness can trigger an active->passive switchover in staging and track state transitions end-to-end
Snapshot restore validation produces deterministic reconciliation report (row counts, CRCs, tombstone reconciliation) and flags drift > 0.1%
Canary fencing logic respects circuit-breaker thresholds and automatically reverts traffic within defined rollback window
Drill run emits metrics to dashboards (slo/latency/cost/restore-time) and generates a post-drill report in Confluence
Playbook updated with runbook steps, roles & responsibilities, and emergency abort procedure
steps: Prototype a modular drill harness (golang service) that can orchestrate region drain, DNS cutover, and traffic shaping
Implement snapshot reconciliation tool: compare manifests, checksums, MVCC timestamps and produce human-readable diff
Add hooks to Canary controller to simulate circuit-breaker firing and test automatic fallback policies
Integrate load-shedding simulator to emulate burst traffic and validate autoscaling and quota enforcement
Create dashboards: drill-latency, restore-duration, error-rate-by-service, and cost-estimate
Author runbook pages and checklist for on-call and SRE leads; schedule the first staged drill in staging and then limited production
progress_updates: 2025-01-22: Kickoff sync with SRE/Platform/PM. Agreed scope: focus on tokenstore + kv-cache + routing policy. Link to notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DR/pages/Failover+Kickoff

2025-01-28: Prototype harness rfc posted. Decided to use existing runner infra (k8s jobs + step functions) to reduce new operational surface. RFC: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDR-DR-RFC

2025-02-01: First snapshot reconciliation tool PoC validated on staging snapshots (3 consecutive snapshots). Found edge-case where tombstone retention caused 0.14% drift — added retention reconciliation step

2025-02-03: Canary fencing tests show expected behavior for 90th percentile latency spike but circuit-breaker threshold needs tuning to avoid thrash. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5123
2025-02-05: Instrumented metrics pipeline to emit drill-specific tags (drill_id, initiator, target_region). Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/DR/drill-overview
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Scheduled drills could accidentally impact production traffic. Mitigation: start in staging, then canary to 1% capacity with kill-switch and manual approval steps
Risk: Snapshot reconciliation slow for large stores. Mitigation: sample-based CRC checks and parallel reconciliation workers; measure Time-To-Check in acceptance criteria
Risk: Circuit-breaker false positives during synthetic load. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum evaluation window; observe for two drills before changing thresholds
Risk: Runbook ambiguity. Mitigation: include explicit abort criteria, contact list, and step-by-step commands with example outputs
next_actions: Finish end-to-end harness wiring and add retries for DNS propagation (owner: Arjun)
Merge reconciliation PoC into tools repo and add parallel worker support (owner: Lina)

postmortem_plan: Collect artifacts: drill logs, reconciliation report, canary traces, dashboard snapshots
Run blameless review within 72 hours, publish action items and owners
Tag follow-ups as separate Linear tickets (data fixes, metric gaps, runbook clarifications)
